children.text:
Know what to do when illness strikes suddenly:

• *Call 000 (Triple Zero):* For severe chest pain, breathing difficulties, or unconsciousness. OSHC includes emergency ambulance transport!

• *ER Reality Check:* Hospital Emergency Rooms (ER) prioritize patients by medical urgency. For mild symptoms, waiting times can be long.

• *Pro-Tip: Medicare Urgent Care Clinics:* Sprains, cuts, or fevers? Medicare Urgent Care Clinics and after-hours GP services treat urgent issues without long ER waits.

• *Healthdirect Hotline:* Call 1800 022 222 anytime for free 24/7 registered nurse advice.
While on campus, a friend collapses, becomes unresponsive, and is struggling to breathe. What is the correct emergency phone number to call in Australia?

data-source.title: Option A
data-source.description: 911 (North American emergency number)

data-source.title: Option B
data-source.description: 999 (United Kingdom emergency number)

data-source.title: Option C
data-source.description: 000 (Triple Zero for emergency services)

data-source.title: Option D
data-source.description: 111 (General non-emergency helpline)

children.text: You experience a sudden, severe medical crisis and require an emergency ambulance to take you to the nearest hospital. How does OSHC generally treat emergency ambulance transport?

data-source.title: Option A
data-source.description: Emergency ambulance transport is not covered by any private health funds

data-source.title: Option B
data-source.description: Emergency ambulance transport is standardly covered when medically necessary

data-source.title: Option C
data-source.description: Ambulances are only covered if booked two weeks in advance by your university

data-source.title: Option D
data-source.description: Transport is covered only if you travel in a private passenger vehicle instead

children.text: Late on a Sunday evening, you twist your ankle playing sports. It is painful and swollen, but you can still move and breathe easily. Regular clinics are closed. What is the most appropriate action?

data-source.title: Option A
data-source.description: Call 000 immediately to request an urgent lights-and-sirens ambulance

data-source.title: Option B
data-source.description: Attend an Urgent Care Clinic or contact an after-hours GP service

data-source.title: Option C
data-source.description: Book an international flight home for routine non-emergency medical care

data-source.title: Option D
data-source.description: Wait two full weeks before mentioning any pain or discomfort to anyone

children.text: A student is deciding between visiting a hospital emergency department and booking an appointment with a local GP. Which symptom clearly warrants going directly to the emergency department?

data-source.title: Option A
data-source.description: A mild headache that started this afternoon after studying

data-source.title: Option B
data-source.description: Severe chest pain, heavy breathing difficulty, or deep uncontrolled bleeding

data-source.title: Option C
data-source.description: A slight runny nose and seasonal sneezing caused by autumn pollen

data-source.title: Option D
data-source.description: Needing a routine dental cleaning or a standard eye examination check

children.text: After being treated and discharged from hospital following a sprained knee, you want an ambulance to drive you back to your rental house because you do not have a car. Is this non-emergency transport covered by OSHC?

data-source.title: Option A
data-source.description: Yes, OSHC provides free routine passenger transport for all university trips

data-source.title: Option B
data-source.description: No, OSHC ambulance benefits exclude non-emergency transport after hospital discharge

data-source.title: Option C
data-source.description: Yes, if the ambulance driver agrees to stop at a grocery market on the way

data-source.title: Option D
data-source.description: No, students are prohibited from traveling in taxis or rideshare cars after injury

children.text:
*Correct Answer:* Option C (000 (Triple Zero for emergency services))

💡 *Explanation:* In Australia, 000 (Triple Zero) is the national emergency telephone number for Ambulance, Police, and Fire services. It is free to call from any mobile or landline in an emergency.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [What you need to know about the Australian healthcare system](https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/understanding-australian-healthcare/)
https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/understanding-australian-healthcare/

*Correct Answer:* Option B (Emergency ambulance transport is standardly covered when medically necessary)

💡 *Explanation:* Standard OSHC policies include cover for emergency ambulance attendance and transport to a hospital when immediate professional medical attention is required and you cannot be safely transported another way.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) | Overseas | Medibank](https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/oshc/)
https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/oshc/

*Correct Answer:* Option B (Attend an Urgent Care Clinic or contact an after-hours GP service)

💡 *Explanation:* For urgent health concerns that are not life-threatening when regular GP clinics are closed, Medicare Urgent Care Clinics, after-hours medical services, or telephone nurse advice lines provide appropriate prompt care without crowding hospital emergency departments.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [What to do if you get sick in Australia](https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/getting-sick-in-australia/)
https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/getting-sick-in-australia/

*Correct Answer:* Option B (Severe chest pain, heavy breathing difficulty, or deep uncontrolled bleeding)

💡 *Explanation:* Hospital emergency departments are designed for critical, life-threatening conditions such as severe chest pain, breathing difficulties, or serious trauma. Mild symptoms and routine checkups should be managed by a GP or community healthcare provider.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [The Australian Healthcare System | Overseas health insurance | Medibank](https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/australian-healthcare/)
https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/australian-healthcare/

*Correct Answer:* Option B (No, OSHC ambulance benefits exclude non-emergency transport after hospital discharge)

💡 *Explanation:* OSHC covers emergency ambulance transport when immediate professional medical attention is required. Routine transport, such as a ride home from the hospital after discharge, is not covered and must be arranged privately (e.g., via taxi, rideshare, or friend).

🔗 *Source Reference:* [Medibank OSHC Member Guide](https://www.medibank.com.au/content/dam/b2c/docs/mpl/Medibank_OSHC_Member_Guide.pdf)
https://www.medibank.com.au/content/dam/b2c/docs/mpl/Medibank_OSHC_Member_Guide.pdf

• *Healthdirect Hotline:* 1800 022 222 (24/7 Registered Nurse advice)
• *Emergency Services:* 000 (Ambulance, Fire, Police - life threats only)
• *National Home Doctor:* 13 74 25 (After-hours bulk-billed home visits)
